text:
Commander night at Tom Beloy's, Saturday 22 August, three-player pod: me on Ur-Dragon, Alex on a mono-red Tannuk, Steadfast Second warp deck, Tom on Merfolk.

Alex played Blood Moon on turn two or three and that was the game. Every nonbasic I own became a Mountain. I could not cast Smothering Tithe, could not cast the red-green dragons, could not cast anything multicoloured. I was reduced to the all-red dragons only.

What I actually did with it: Moltensteel Dragon, and at the end I paid sixteen life to pump it and hit Alex for twelve. If I was locked out anyway, he was going to feel it.

Blood Moon is a broken card in my view and I am not building around it. At bracket 3+ some people run that stuff and that is the deal. So I am not calling this a deck problem in the sense of needing an answer to Blood Moon.

The real lesson is the mana base and I want it audited holistically: how many basics I run and whether land tutors can whiff, whether the pip spread across the lands actually matches what the dragons demand rather than just being generic fixing, and whether I am taking tempo hits from enters-tapped lands where an untapped source would do. Tap lands are fine to a degree.

The rest of the deck I am happy with - removal, treasures, discounts, haste, card draw are all solid. The bottleneck is mana consistency, not card selection.
